newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik leader to reduce armed forces by 30 percent.
newsitem.headline: Tajik leader to reduce armed forces by 30 percent.

text.p: Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov has ordered a 30 percent reduction in the former Soviet republic's armed forces, state television said on Thursday.
"The President's decree proposes a reduction of 30 percent," Tajik state television reported.
Rakhmonov's decree is a further sign that the remote Central Asian state bordering Afghanistan and China is tentatively emerging from a devastating four-year civil war which killed tens of thousands.
The Tajik leader shook hands with the chief of his Islamic foes in Moscow last month after signing a peace deal. A ceasefire has held since last December.
The broadcast said the cuts would be made to interior and defence ministry troops, the presidential guard, a rapid reaction force and the committees for emergency situations and civil defence.
An official in Rakhmonov's administration, who declined to be named, confirmed the decree to Reuters. "We're talking about reducing the armed forces by about 5,000 men," he said.
But the report did not say whether the decree was aimed at making room for opposition guerrillas who under the peace deal must either lay down their weapons or join a new state force.
State television said the money saved would go to paying teachers and medical workers.

Earlier this week, the head of Russia's border guards, General Andrei Nikolayev, said that while the peace accord had changed the situation in the country "radically", it would be several months before a reduction in Russian forces would be considered.
A potential flashpoint is the return of guerrillas to the republic from bases in neighbouring Afghanistan -- Nikolayev said no armed people would be allowed to cross the border.
Russia deploys some 20,000 soldiers in the Central Asian state. They guard the remote, mountainous frontiers and perform peacekeeping duties, viewing themselves as a bulwark against militant Islam.
